title: Algorithmic Governance & Constitutional Safeguards in Arab Legal Systems
abstract: This study examines the constitutional implications of automated decision-making and artificial intelligence deployment in judicial administrative processes across MENA jurisdictions. It proposes a human-centric regulatory model balancing digital transformation with fundamental rights.
fullDescription: Artificial intelligence integration within judicial and regulatory systems presents profound constitutional challenges, particularly concerning due process, transparency, and non-discrimination. This comprehensive paper analyzes recent legal reforms in Egypt, UAE, and Saudi Arabia, offering a comparative legal doctrine for algorithmic accountability.
journalOrPublisher: Middle East Law and Governance Review (Vol. 18, Issue 3)

title: Public Policy Exceptions in MENA International Commercial Arbitration: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: An empirical analysis of annulment decisions based on public policy (Ordre Public) in commercial arbitration enforcement across Cairo, Dubai, and Riyadh arbitral institutions.
fullDescription: The defense of public policy remains one of the most litigated and unpredictable grounds for setting aside arbitral awards in Arab countries. This study categorizes judicial interpretations over a 15-year period, identifying trends towards international harmony.
journalOrPublisher: Journal of International Dispute Settlement (Oxford Academic)

title: Reconceptualizing Property Rights in Digital Assets under Civil Law Traditions
abstract: Exploring how classical civil law property concepts can be adapted to accommodate digital tokens, smart contracts, and decentralized data assets.
fullDescription: Civil law jurisdictions traditionally require tangible possession or explicit statutory creation for property rights. This monograph proposes an architectural amendment to civil codes allowing in rem rights over cryptographic protocols.
journalOrPublisher: Cambridge University Press (Monograph Series on Comparative Law)
